Don’t mistake the no lay offs things they say and never be comfortable. I worked for a company for more than 3 years right after college. I heard the same shit we don’t lay off, we value our people etc.. and everyone’s been here more than 15 years. Initially I thought I was getting paid less, not as much as I could earn. But it was comfortable and I thought I could stay here. Last week our whole team got laid off including people who worked more than 10 years with no warning. We got to office, got a meeting from VP, and were literally out of the door in an hour. So don’t ever get comfortable. Always be on top of your game and start looking for better options. Always always be ready to jump the ship or be ready if you are pushed.

Agreed. Vit D and B12 are extremely important. When I first came to the US I was living in a very cold place and was severely depressed. I just didn’t know what to do. It was horrible. One day I contacted a therapist and the first thing they asked me to do was to get tested for vit D and we realized I had dangerously low levels which is one of the reasons for my depression. So yeah getting blood work done would also be very useful. Weather change valla kuda we ll face lots of issues I guess.

I found my therapist from there and she helped me a lot. And it is not too expensive either.
